title.en: Gravitational potential energy and escape speed
title.kn: ಗುರುತ್ವ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಮತ್ತು ವಿಮೋಚನಾ ವೇಗ

heading.en: How fast to leave the earth for good?
heading.kn: ಭೂಮಿಯನ್ನು ಶಾಶ್ವತವಾಗಿ ಬಿಡಲು ಎಷ್ಟು ವೇಗ ಬೇಕು?

hook.en: Throw a ball up and it comes back. Throw it faster and it goes higher. Is there a speed at which it never returns? Yes: about 11.2 km/s.
hook.kn: ಚೆಂಡನ್ನು ಮೇಲೆಸೆದರೆ ಅದು ಹಿಂತಿರುಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಇನ್ನೂ ವೇಗವಾಗಿ ಎಸೆದರೆ ಇನ್ನೂ ಎತ್ತರಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಹಿಂತಿರುಗದ ವೇಗ ಇದೆಯೇ? ಹೌದು, ಸುಮಾರು 11.2 km/s.

narration.en: Throw a ball up and it comes back. Throw it faster and it goes higher. Is there a speed at which it never returns? Yes: about 11.2 km/s.
narration.kn: ಚೆಂಡನ್ನು ಮೇಲೆಸೆದರೆ ಅದು ಹಿಂತಿರುಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಇನ್ನೂ ವೇಗವಾಗಿ ಎಸೆದರೆ ಇನ್ನೂ ಎತ್ತರಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಹಿಂತಿರುಗದ ವೇಗ ಇದೆಯೇ? ಹೌದು, ಸುಮಾರು 11.2 km/s.

body.en: Far from the surface, mgh no longer works because g changes. Taking the potential energy to be zero at infinity, the potential energy of a mass m at distance r from the centre of the earth is $V(r) = -GM_Em/r$. It is negative because gravity is attractive: work must be done to pull the mass away to infinity. The gravitational potential is $V/m = -GM_E/r$.
body.kn: ಮೇಲ್ಮೈಯಿಂದ ದೂರದಲ್ಲಿ g ಬದಲಾಗುವುದರಿಂದ mgh ಅನ್ವಯಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಅನಂತದಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಶೂನ್ಯ ಎಂದು ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಂಡರೆ, r ದೂರದಲ್ಲಿ V = −GMm/r. ಗುರುತ್ವ ಆಕರ್ಷಕವಾದ್ದರಿಂದ ಇದು ಋಣ.

points.en: mgh is the small-height form of this result
V rises (becomes less negative) as r increases

narration.en: Far from the surface, mgh no longer works because g changes. Taking the potential energy to be zero at infinity, the potential energy of a mass m at distance r from the centre of the earth is $V(r) = -GM_Em/r$. It is negative because gravity is attractive: work must be done to pull the mass away to infinity. The gravitational potential is $V/m = -GM_E/r$.
narration.kn: ಮೇಲ್ಮೈಯಿಂದ ದೂರದಲ್ಲಿ g ಬದಲಾಗುವುದರಿಂದ mgh ಅನ್ವಯಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಅನಂತದಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಶೂನ್ಯ ಎಂದು ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಂಡರೆ, r ದೂರದಲ್ಲಿ V = −GMm/r. ಗುರುತ್ವ ಆಕರ್ಷಕವಾದ್ದರಿಂದ ಇದು ಋಣ.

say.en: Far from the earth, mgh fails. Taking zero at infinity, the potential energy is minus G M m over r: negative because gravity attracts.
To escape, the kinetic energy at launch must at least cancel the negative potential energy at the surface.
For the earth, the escape speed is about 11.2 kilometres per second, whatever the mass or the direction of launch.

narration.en: On the board: Potential energy and escape speed.

body.en: The escape speed is the least speed with which a body must be projected from the surface to reach infinity. Setting $\tfrac12 mv_e^2 = GM_Em/R_E$ gives $v_e = \sqrt{2GM_E/R_E} = \sqrt{2gR_E} \approx 11.2$ km/s for the earth. It does not depend on the mass of the body or the direction of projection. On the Moon it is only about 2.3 km/s, which is why the Moon has no atmosphere.
body.kn: ಮೇಲ್ಮೈಯಿಂದ ಎಸೆದ ಕಾಯ ಅನಂತವನ್ನು ತಲುಪಲು ಬೇಕಾದ ಕನಿಷ್ಠ ವೇಗವೇ ವಿಮೋಚನಾ ವೇಗ: v_e = √(2gR) ≈ 11.2 km/s. ಇದು ಕಾಯದ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಅಥವಾ ಎಸೆಯುವ ದಿಕ್ಕನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಚಂದ್ರನ ಮೇಲೆ ಅದು ಸುಮಾರು 2.3 km/s; ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಚಂದ್ರನಿಗೆ ವಾತಾವರಣವಿಲ್ಲ.

problem.en: How much energy is needed to take a 100 kg satellite from the earth's surface to infinity? (g = 9.8 m/s², R_E = 6.4 × 10⁶ m)

steps.en: Needed energy = 0 − (−GM_E m/R_E) = GM_E m/R_E = mgR_E.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. How much energy is needed to take a 100 kg satellite from the earth's surface to infinity? (g = 9.8 m/s², R_E = 6.4 × 10⁶ m)

body.en: v_e = √(2GM/R). For planets of the same density, M ∝ R³, so v_e ∝ R: a planet with twice the radius and the same density has twice the escape speed.

narration.en: How escape speed scales. v_e = √(2GM/R). For planets of the same density, M ∝ R³, so v_e ∝ R: a planet with twice the radius and the same density has twice the escape speed.
